2.1a — Coins: Triggers, Tags & the StatManager

Collecting a coin is the first real event in your game: two objects meet, code runs, state changes, and the world updates. One pickup pattern, reused all year — learn it once here.

Predict First ~10 min

Read the pickup half of PlayerController.cs:

private void OnTriggerEnter2D(Collider2D other)
{
    if (other.CompareTag("Coin"))
    {
        if (StatManager.manager != null)
        {
            StatManager.manager.ChangeCoins(1);
        }
        Destroy(other.gameObject);
    }
}

Predict: the coin spins in place until you touch it. Which object runs this code — the coin or the player? And when it says Destroy(other.gameObject), which object vanishes? What would happen if it destroyed gameObject (no "other.") instead?

Socratic

ChangeCoins(1) increments a counter that lives on a completely different object, the StatManager — a singleton that survives scene loads. Why not just keep coins as a field on the Player? What breaks the moment the player dies and the Start scene reloads?

Build Lab ~25 min

Step 1 — rebuild the handler. Comment out the coin branch in OnTriggerEnter2D, then retype it in three lines: check the tag, tell the StatManager, destroy the coin. Run the game between each line: after line 1 you can walk through coins silently; after line 2 the Console counts but the coin survives; after line 3 the whole pattern is back. One line = one responsibility — that is why it feels clean.

Step 2 — read the money printer. Open StatManager.cs and find the method your line calls:

public void ChangeCoins(int amount)
{
    coins += amount;
    Debug.Log("Coins Changed! New Total: " + coins);
}

One plus sign and a log line. The Console is your scoreboard for now — the UI comes later. Trace it: what does ChangeCoins(-1) do, and when will you use that in a shop, someday?

Step 3 — verify the tag. Select a Coin prefab (Assets/Prefabs). Its Inspector has a Tag field at the top: it says Coin, a custom tag someone added in the tag list. Trigger + tag is the whole identification system: no names, no references, just "are you one of the things I care about?"

Bug Hunt: Silence is the enemy

  1. Change the code's tag to compareTag("coin") (lowercase). Play. What happens — and why is a typo'd tag the most silent bug in Unity?
  2. Clear the Coin tag in the Inspector (set it to Untagged). Now what happens, and what does that say about where identity actually lives?
  3. Comment out the Destroy line. Why is "the counter is right but the coin is still there" a worse game than the first bug?
  4. Walk into a spike instead of a coin. Why does nothing print — and which handler would spikes need instead? (Tomorrow's whole lesson: see 2.2a.)
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Make the pickup yours

  1. Add a second coin value: big coins. Give the prefab a different tag ("BigCoin"), a bigger sprite, and pass 5 instead of 1. What changed in the handler — one branch or two?
  2. The StatManager logs "Coins Changed!" — make it print the total only, with no words. Which line did you touch, and who else sees that change?
  3. Make coins play a sound instead of only logging. (Hint: the prefab needs an AudioSource + one line of code you will have to find. Note the approach for later units.)

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Write the pickup pattern from memory: trigger → tag → change state → destroy
  • Say which object runs OnTriggerEnter2D and what other refers to
  • Explain why a singleton StatManager beats a player field for coins
  • Debug a silent tag mismatch in under a minute
